source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 954 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 954 was established by Ordinance No. 29981, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 13, 2016. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 954 is established on property located on the south side of Coronado Avenue, east of Grand Avenue. The size of PD 954 is approximately 1.561 acres. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A. In this article, STOOP means a small porch leading to the entrance of a residence.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 954A: development plan. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 954A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District, as set out

in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District is subject to DIR in this district; etc. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MF-2(A) Multifamily District apply.

(b) Multifamily.

(1) Front yard.

(A) Minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(B) Encroachments of stairs, steps, stoops, unenclosed balconies and porches, awnings, and canopies may project up to five feet into the required front yard.

(2) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yard is 10 feet.

(3) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 100.

(4) Height.

(A) Maximum structure height is 78 feet.

(B) The following structures may project a maximum of 12 feet above the maximum structure height:

(i) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead.

(ii) Mechanical equipment room.

(iii) Cooling tower.

(iv) Tank designed to hold liquids.

(v) Skylights.

(vi) Clerestory.

(vii) Visual screens that surround roof mounted mechanical equipment.

(viii) Chimney and vent stacks.

(ix) Parapet wall limited to four feet in height.

(5) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(6) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is seven. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Multifamily. For a multifamily use, one space per bedroom is required up to a maximum of two spaces per dwelling unit. An additional 0.25 off-street parking space per dwelling unit must be provided for guest parking.

(c) Parking structure screening.

(1) Street-facing parking structure facades must be similar in appearance to the facade of the main structure or the adjacent structure, except that breaks in the exterior parking structure facade not exceeding 40 feet in width are permitted at driveway and entryway locations. Cable guard strands and chain link fencing are prohibited on the street-facing facade of a parking structure.

(2) Openings in the street-facing parking structure facade may not exceed 60 percent of the total parking structure facade area. A street-facing parking structure must have solid screening at least 42 inches in height on each floor level within the parking structure to screen vehicles and vehicle headlights.

(3) This subsection does not apply to individual garages attached to a single dwelling unit. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.112. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Streets And Pedestrian Amenities
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.113. STREETS AND PEDESTRIAN AMENITIES.

(a) Coronado Avenue. Minimum right-of-way width is 53 feet.

(b) Sidewalk. Minimum sidewalk width is five feet.

(c) Pedestrian amenities. A minimum of two of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided along the street frontage:

(1) Benches.

(2) Trash receptacles.

(3) Publicly accessible bicycle rack.

(d) Pedestrian-scale lighting.

(1) Pedestrian light standards must be provided along all public rights-of-way and must have a maximum spacing of 50 feet.

(2) Pedstrian light standards may not be less than nine feet nor more than 15 feet in height above a sidewalk or pathway. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29981)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-954.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29981)
